sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The linking vowel copies the vowels of the word. A word with back vowels (*a, á, o, ó, u, ú*) takes *-ok*; a word with front vowels (*e, é, i, í*) takes *-ek*. In a word with mixed vowels the last vowel decides: *telefon* ends in *o*, so *telefonok*. (A few words with *ö* or *ü* take *-ök*; you will meet them when they come.)

items.spanish: A székek és az ablakok itt vannak.
items.english: The chairs and the windows are here.

sections.content: You do not need to memorise which noun takes which ending. Say the word and listen: *asztal* and *barát* sound dark, *szék* and *ember* sound bright, and the ending follows.
